history.dynasty: No ruling dynasty; funded privately by a devotee (Pisanhari), a flour-grinder
history.period: 1442 CE (original temple; later temples added over centuries)
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN (DIGAMBARA) TEMPLE COMPLEX, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Pisanhari Ki Madiya is a major Digambara Jain tirtha on a 300-foot hill near Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Medical College, Jabalpur. Legend says it was built in 1442 CE by a poor woman called Pisanhari who saved her earnings from grinding flour; her statue stands at the entrance and her grinding stones are preserved above the gateway. The complex now spans ~18 acres with 13+ temples including a cave shrine, the Shri Nandishwar Dweep Jinalaya (152 marble Tirthankara idols), a Manastambha, a Samavsaran Mandir, and a 55-foot Bahubali statue. NOTE CONFLICTS: Wikipedia names Parshvanatha as the deity, while travel sources say the main shrine houses Adinatha; one source dates the two oldest idols to 1587 rather than 1442. Coordinates approximate (hilltop complex).

town_description: Jabalpur is a major city in Madhya Pradesh on the banks of the Narmada, famous for the marble rocks and Dhuandhar falls at Bhedaghat. It was an important British cantonment and arms-manufacturing centre (Gun Carriage Factory, ordnance factories). Today it is the region's educational, administrative and industrial hub.
